scores.claim_text: Company has expanded its high-density colocation contract with CoreWeave to approximately 590 MW of leased customer power capacity through the exercise of contractual options during 2024 and into early 2025.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Core Scientific' (no CIK): 1126 hits — strong external presence including 8-Ks dated 2025-10-14 (likely merger termination)
edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'CoreWeave' (no CIK): 434 hits — top filing is CoreWeave's own 10-Q (CRWV, CIK 0001769628), confirming CoreWeave is now a public registrant

edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Core Scientific' (cik=0001769628 CoreWeave): 10 hits — CoreWeave's own 8-Ks (2025-07-07 merger announcement, 2025-10-31 termination, 2025-07-21) and 10-Q dated 2025-08-13 all reference Core Scientific. Counterparty-side corroboration is HARD
scores.M_check: Layer 3 Rule 7 (counterparty disclosure). CoreWeave was treated as private/UNVERIFIABLE in the calibration heuristic but IPO'd ahead of the cutoff (ticker CRWV, CIK 0001769628). Counterparty test now possible and PASSES — CoreWeave's own filings reference Core Scientific 10 times before cutoff.
scores.interpretation: The 590 MW colocation relationship is corroborated bilaterally — CORZ discloses it and CoreWeave discloses it (including the failed July-October 2025 acquisition attempt that further bonds the two counterparties). PASS on counterparty corroboration. Note Calibration Heuristic 3 caution: 590 MW is leased capacity, not energized/billable capacity, and most of the 2025 revenue was still from BTC self-mining — but the claim itself is about contractual capacity, not current revenue.

scores.claim_text: Company operates 10 data centers across 7 U.S. states totaling 1.4 GW gross utility power capacity (1,426 MW) and 920 MW total leasable customer power capacity as of December 31, 2025.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Denton' (cik=0001839341 CORZ): 91 hits — Denton TX (CORZ's largest site at 394 MW gross) is extensively self-disclosed across 8-Ks, 10-Ks, and 10-Qs from 2023 through 2026
edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Marble' (no CIK): 2017 hits — name too common (matches REIT and other filers); the Marble NC site corroboration is non-discriminative
scores.M_check: Internal disclosure consistency for the largest site (Denton TX, 394 MW). Per-site MW breakdown by utility provider in 10-K sums to 1,426 MW gross — matches the 1.4 GW claim arithmetically.
scores.M_value: n_corz_denton_hits=91; per-utility MW sum from 10-K table = 1,426 MW (matches '1.4 GW' headline)
scores.interpretation: Facility table in Item 1 lists every site, electric utility provider, and MW capacity by location, summing to 1,426 MW gross — arithmetically consistent with the 1.4 GW headline. Denton TX (the largest site) is extensively cross-referenced in prior CORZ filings. PASS. Note: the claim that 'a portion' are in operation while 'the remainder' are under construction is honest stage-ladder disclosure; specific operating-vs-under-construction MW split is NOT broken out in the slice, which is a mild disclosure-quality gap but not a contradiction.

scores.claim_text: Company has $989.8 million of contractually committed capital expenditures as of December 31, 2025 (with $716.8M passed through to customer as invoiced), plus an additional $418.1 million committed through February 26, 2026; expected to occur within 12-24 months.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Core Scientific' (cik=0001839341): 662 hits including the most recent 10-K — the filing footprint is internally consistent
10-K MD&A discloses 2025 capex actually spent = $729.0M (vs $95.0M in 2024); investing cash outflow = $740.8M; PP&E construction-in-progress jumped from $112.0M to $911.1M
Liquidity disclosure: cash and cash equivalents fell from $836.2M (12/31/24) to $311.4M (12/31/25); BTC treasury $222.0M; mgmt plans to monetize substantially all BTC in Q1 2026 to fund capex
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 9 (TCV vs current-period revenue conflation) AND Heuristic 10 (post-emergence balance sheet stress). $989.8M committed + $418.1M subsequent = $1,407.9M committed against $311M cash + $222M BTC (~$533M liquidity) + $716.8M expected to be invoiced through to customer. Net company-funded capex exposure ~$691M against ~$533M cash-plus-BTC, with operating cash flow of $278M in 2025 (driven by deferred-revenue/customer-prepayment build, not operating profitability — Adj EBITDA only $29.7M).
scores.M_value: committed_capex=$1407.9M; pass-through_to_customer=$716.8M (CORZ commits 12/31)+$107.4M (subsequent)=$824.2M; CORZ net commitment ≈ $583.7M; available liquidity ≈ $533M cash+BTC at year-end; net cash from operations = $278M in 2025 (but Adj EBITDA only $29.7M)
scores.interpretation: Capex commitments are real and disclosed in good faith, BUT the financing math is tight: net company-funded capex (~$584M after pass-through to customer) materially exceeds year-end cash+BTC (~$533M). Mgmt's 'next 12 months sufficient liquidity' assertion depends on (a) monetizing essentially all BTC treasury in Q1 2026, (b) continuing customer prepayments, and (c) likely additional external financing. Cap-ex risk + heavy dependence on a single customer's prepayment stream = MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY risk.

scores.claim_text: Colocation segment revenue is 100% concentrated with a single customer (Customer J = CoreWeave); Customer F became a minority shareholder on the Effective Date and was 31% of Digital Asset Hosted Mining revenue in 2025.
supports: Filing itself: 'Colocation segment revenue is concentrated with a single customer' and segment-revenue table shows Customer J = 100% of Colocation revenue in BOTH 2025 and 2024
edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'CoreWeave' (cik=0001018724 Amazon): 0 hits — Amazon does NOT mention CoreWeave

edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'CoreWeave' (cik=0000789019 Microsoft): 0 hits — Microsoft does NOT mention CoreWeave by name in EDGAR filings either (despite being CoreWeave's largest end customer per industry reporting). This means CoreWeave's revenue base is itself opaque to public investors at the hyperscaler-disclosure layer
Per C1: CoreWeave (CRWV) is now public and DOES disclose Core Scientific; counterparty corroboration of the relationship exists
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern + circular relationships) + Heuristic 7 (counterparty disclosure). Bilateral CoreWeave-CORZ corroboration EXISTS (C1), but the single-customer concentration creates downstream concentration risk: if CoreWeave loses Microsoft (its primary end-customer) or CoreWeave's growth stalls, 100% of CORZ's colocation backlog evaporates. Also: failed July-October 2025 acquisition by the SAME customer raises governance/conflict considerations.
scores.M_value: colocation_customer_count=1 (Customer J); colocation_customer_concentration=100% (both 2025 and 2024); failed acquisition by same counterparty 7/2025-10/2025; $21.6M merger advisory fees burned
scores.interpretation: Customer-concentration risk is acknowledged in the filing (good disclosure), but the substantive risk is SEVERE: (1) 100% of the AI/HDC pivot rides on one private counterparty; (2) that counterparty just attempted and failed to acquire CORZ, leaving the commercial relationship intact but the strategic relationship strained; (3) hyperscaler downstream demand (Microsoft) does not even acknowledge CoreWeave in 10-K commentary, meaning CORZ has TWO layers of opacity in front of its eventual demand. Score SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY on the implicit claim that this represents a derisked, durable pivot.

scores.claim_text: Total revenue declined to $319.0 million in 2025 from $510.7 million in 2024; Adjusted EBITDA collapsed to $29.7 million in 2025 from $157.4 million in 2024; operating loss expanded to $245.6 million from $142.1 million; net loss $288.6 million.
supports: Filing MD&A: revenue $319.0M (2025) vs $510.7M (2024) = -37.5% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA: $29.7M (2025) vs $157.4M (2024) = -81% YoY
Hashrate context: 15.7 EH/s self-mining at 12/31/25 vs 19.1 EH/s at 12/31/24 (down ~18%), and self-miner count fell from ~164,000 to ~135,500 as facilities converted away from BTC
Bitcoin range in 2025: $74,485 - $126,210, average $101,639 — BTC price was actually STRONG in 2025; the revenue decline is driven by self-mining fleet reduction (conversion), not BTC weakness
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 11 (legacy BTC mining revenue is volatile and not equivalent to AI-hosting revenue). The 'pivot' is causing a hard revenue cliff: BTC revenue is being intentionally reduced faster than colocation revenue is ramping. Colocation revenue was 'partially offset' but clearly not enough — net decline ~$192M revenue, ~$128M Adj EBITDA evaporation.
scores.M_value: revenue_decline_yoy=-37.5%; adj_ebitda_decline_yoy=-81%; op_loss_expansion=+73%; self_miner_count_decline=-17.4%; hashrate_decline=-17.8%; BTC_avg_price_2025=$101,639 (strong)
scores.interpretation: This is the central financial-distress signal: the company is mid-pivot and the new business (HDC/colocation) is not yet generating enough revenue to replace the legacy business (BTC mining) that is being dismantled. With $1.4B+ committed capex and ~$533M liquidity, the operating-loss trajectory means CORZ has roughly 12-18 months of runway before requiring substantial external financing. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY on the implicit claim that the AI/HDC pivot is a smooth handoff.

scores.claim_text: Company identified a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025 related to accounting for demolished property/equipment during HDC conversion; concurrently filing a restated 10-K/A for FY2024 and 10-Q/As for Q1/Q2/Q3 2025. KPMG issued an adverse opinion on ICFR.
supports: Filing Item 9A: 'our internal control over financial reporting was not effective due to the material weakness described below'

Filing Note 3: 'Restatement of Previously Issued Financial Statements' — errors related to accounting for property, plant and equipment demolished in connection with the conversion of certain facilities from digital asset mining to HDC
Concurrent filing of 10-K/A for FY2024 and 10-Q/As for ALL THREE 2025 interim periods
Auditor KPMG LLP issued an ADVERSE OPINION on the effectiveness of internal control
Disclosure controls also deemed not effective by CEO/CFO
PP&E line items affected: 'Mining and network equipment' (mid-conversion), 'Building and improvements', impairment recognition timing — directly tied to the entire HDC pivot narrative
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 10 (going-concern/control fingerprints) hard trigger. A post-emergence company with an adverse ICFR opinion AND a four-period restatement AND material weakness AND a restated FY2024 (its first full post-emergence year) is exhibiting clear financial-reporting distress. The restatement is specifically about the conversion process — meaning the central strategic claim (mass HDC conversion) is the same thing that the controls failed to account for properly.
scores.M_value: material_weakness_flag=TRUE; restated_periods=4 (FY24 10-K/A + Q1/Q2/Q3 2025 10-Q/A); auditor_adverse_opinion_on_ICFR=TRUE; disclosure_controls_ineffective=TRUE; remediation_in_progress=TRUE (not yet remediated)
scores.interpretation: RED FLAG. This is a textbook combination: (a) restated post-emergence financials, (b) adverse auditor opinion on ICFR, (c) material weakness directly in the asset class being most aggressively transformed (PP&E conversion from BTC to HDC), and (d) disclosure controls also ineffective. Per Heuristic 10, this is a hard fingerprint of distress and a forward-looking risk that the conversion-related capex disclosures could themselves be subject to further restatement.

scores.claim_text: Proposed CoreWeave all-stock acquisition of Core Scientific (announced July 7, 2025) was terminated October 30, 2025 following CORZ stockholder rejection at special meeting; Company incurred $21.6 million in advisory fees.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'CoreWeave' (cik=0001839341 CORZ): 68 hits including 8-Ks dated 2025-07-07 (announcement), 2025-10-14 and 2025-10-15 (likely proxy/voting), and 2026-04-21
From C1 query: CoreWeave's own 8-Ks dated 2025-07-07 (announcement) and 2025-10-31 (termination) confirm bilateral disclosure
DEFM14A filing 0001140361-25-036346 appears in CORZ filings index, consistent with definitive proxy for the merger vote
scores.M_check: Bilateral M&A disclosure consistency. Both CORZ (68 internal CoreWeave references) and CoreWeave (10 Core Scientific references) corroborate the announcement-to-termination arc. The dollar amount of advisory fees ($21.6M) is plausible for an all-stock public-co merger of this size and was charged through P&L in 2025.
scores.interpretation: PASS — the merger and termination are extensively documented across both companies' EDGAR footprints. This is a clean fact pattern; the only downstream concern is the strategic awkwardness that CORZ's sole material customer just attempted to buy CORZ and was rejected by CORZ's own shareholders, which is captured under C4.

scores.claim_text: In January 2026 (subsequent event), Company entered a long-term power supply arrangement obligating it to purchase firm utility power capacity beginning in 2028; made an $80 million cash deposit into restricted escrow.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Core Scientific' (cik=0001839341, forms=8-K): 520 hits with broad 8-K activity
10-K subsequent events section discloses the $80M escrow deposit and the 2028 power supply commitment
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational): the new power capacity is firm but doesn't come online until 2028 — that is 2+ years of cash tied up before it produces any revenue, against the backdrop of $311M cash at YE 2025 falling further as Q1 2026 BTC sales occur. Heuristic 9 (TCV vs current revenue): no current-period economic benefit, but $80M of liquidity is now locked.
scores.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The disclosure itself is honest, but the move further stresses liquidity: an additional $80M restricted (on top of $1.4B in committed capex) for capacity that does not generate revenue until 2028. This is consistent with growing reliance on customer prepayments and BTC monetization to fund near-term operations. The 2028 start date also means the company will need to secure ADDITIONAL customer demand (beyond CoreWeave) to absorb that future capacity — or this $80M becomes a stranded-asset risk.

scores.claim_text: Company holds 2,537 bitcoin worth $222.0 million at year-end 2025; intends to monetize substantially all bitcoin holdings during 2026 (mostly Q1) to fund planned capex; already sold 1,924 BTC for $175.9 million between January 1 and February 26, 2026.
supports: 10-K MD&A liquidity section explicitly states: 'we currently expect to monetize substantially all of our bitcoin holdings... to enhance liquidity and fund our planned capital expenditures and other cash requirements'
10-K subsequent events: 1,924 BTC sold for $175.9M aggregate proceeds = ~$91,400/BTC avg sale price (within 2025 BTC range of $74,485-$126,210)
Remaining post-Feb 2026: ~613 BTC (~$56M at January 2026 prices, less if BTC sold off)
Tied to C3 (capex commitment) and C5 (revenue/EBITDA collapse) — the BTC sale is the marginal funding source
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 10 (distress fingerprints) + Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern). A BTC miner is meant to ACCUMULATE BTC as long-duration treasury reserve; monetizing essentially the entire BTC stack within one quarter to fund operations is a hard distress signal. It also forfeits the embedded option value of BTC appreciation during a year when CORZ's HDC revenue is still small.
scores.M_value: btc_held_at_yearend=2537; btc_value=$222.0M; btc_sold_post_yearend=1924 (76% of stack); btc_sale_proceeds=$175.9M; intent_to_monetize_substantially_all=TRUE; capex_commitments_to_cover=$1407.9M
scores.interpretation: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY. Selling 76% of the BTC stack in <2 months and stating intent to sell substantially all of it during 2026 is a clear forced-liquidation pattern, not a treasury-management decision. Combined with cash decline ($836M -> $311M YoY) and material weakness/restatement, this puts CORZ in a position where any colocation revenue shortfall, customer prepayment delay, or capex overrun would require additional external financing on bad terms — and CORZ already burned $21.6M on a failed merger. Distress signal.

scores.claim_text: Company has filed over 130 patent applications in technologies such as blockchain, data center management, infrastructure and cooling; a subset have been granted.
supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee 'Core Scientific': 132 total applications (matches '>130' claim), 60 granted ('Patented Case' status) — substantial granted-patent subset confirms 'a subset have been granted'

Sample titles in returned list include: 'SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR USING WASTE HEAT FROM COMPUTING DEVICES', 'HEAT SINK THAT VARIES IN HEIGHT', 'SYSTEM FOR COOLING COMPUTING DEVICES IN AN ARRAY' — corroborates the cooling and data-center management subject claim
CPC codes (H05K 7/20*, F24H 15/*) align with data-center thermal management and waste-heat utilization
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 8 (patent estate is typically light for AI-DC pure-plays; absence not a red flag). CORZ actually exceeds the threshold — 60 granted patents pre-cutoff is unusually strong for an AI-DC pivot company. This is one of CORZ's more credible competitive moats.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=132 (matches '>130' claim within rounding); n_granted=60; cooling_thermal_titles_present=TRUE; datacenter_titles_present=TRUE
scores.interpretation: PASS. Patent disclosure is materially accurate and the technology areas (cooling, waste heat, rack thermal management) align with the AI/HPC pivot narrative. This is one of the few unambiguously credible elements of the AI-DC story.
